description:
STATUS (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1): LIVE WRONG ANSWER on interp,
refusal on native. Reproducer (session scratchpad sl3.fz):

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(1), 10))     # means 12   -- interp prints 12.0
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(0.5), 10))   # means 11.0 -- interp prints 11.0
  end

Both call orders; the int call is always wrong. Native: "closure capture
0 of callable 69 has no single settled representation".

THE MINT IS EXACT (this corrects the two earlier bodies of this ticket).
A closure value's code word names its CONSTRUCTION WRAPPER: one per
producer position, carrying 'callable: CallableId' = CallableDescr
(function, arity, capture_tys, capture_shapes, capture_lanes). Native
stamps a fresh identity_fn per wrapper (jobs/native.rs:126, mint :3591;
codegen's callable_boundary_for_identity is 1:1); interp stamps
0x8000_0000|wrapper (ir_interp/backend.rs:1995). In sl3 the two closures
carry DIFFERENT words on both doors. 00411 (same lambda at int/float,
no forwarder, indirect calls through the word) is green on native.

THE PROGRAM IS STATIC. Every call site in main knows which closure it
passes. The need for any runtime question is MANUFACTURED by the fz-6gb
forwarder erasure: World::canonical_activation_key -> Types::erase_
transported_closure_identities -> erase_closure_identity -> Descr::
without_closure_lits drops the closure literal WHOLE -- brand AND capture
types (arity survives) -- so run is one body '(a0_p0) -> a0_r' for two
callers whose consumers (twice[closure[L](int)] / [(float)]) were never
going to be shared, and the only way left to un-merge them is a test at
run's callsite. Then every reader of that test is keyed on ClosureTarget
= FnId (types/closure.rs:18) and cannot ask it:
 1. callable_identity_clauses (types/mod.rs:2680-2700) emits captures:
    Vec::new(); callable_identity_targets (:2410) reads only lit.fn_id.
    One predicate for both -> no question -> 'graph root=n1 -> outcome
    o0' -> arm 0 (twice[float]) takes the int closure. Interp: int
    capture into a RawF64 lane; AnyValue::as_float accepts Int under the
    F64 extern marshal (fz-kdt.164), 10+1.0 = 11.0 then 12.0.
 2. Native callable_addresses (prim.rs:1370) ORs every wrapper with
    target == fn (surface.rs:85 callable_boundaries_for_target).
 3. Interp backend_callable_identity (ir_interp/backend.rs:622-633)
    drops wrapper.callable.
 4. The ClosureCapture emitter (jobs/native.rs:3850) holds the exact
    CallableId and coarsens it to ClosureTarget(function);
    lower_closure_capture (prim.rs:1138) demands one repr across ALL
    wrappers of the fn -> the refusal. Interp: no typed unpack; :2784
    exempts wrapper words from its function check.
 5. NativeCallableBoundary.target: Option<ClosureTarget> (artifact.rs:
    370) drops the CallableId (jobs/native.rs:200-203).

PRINCIPLE (user review, 2026-09-02): runtime tests are the LAST resort.
Static knowledge flows by KEY; dynamic knowledge flows by the WORD the
mint stamped. No test re-derives what a key or the word already says.

COLD REVIEW VERDICT (2026-09-02, scratchpad review/verdict.md):
ACCEPT-WITH-CHANGES on the amended two-population shape; BOTH halves
prototyped on all three doors (worktree wt-kdt127-review, protoA/protoB/
protoAB.diff, clippy clean): A+B prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT, AOT,
both orders, with ZERO dispatch nodes. Changes forced by evidence:
 1. ORDER IS (B) THEN (A). The dynamic witness (closure chosen by a
    runtime case, then run(f,10)) is CORRECT at base on every door
    (one erased run body, union input, indirect call through the word)
    and (A) ALONE MAKES IT WRONG (interp 12 then an extern Int fault;
    JIT/AOT refuse): A splits run into two keys and main's callsite
    becomes a 2-target dispatch in this very shape. (B) answers it there.
 2. ADMISSION IS CONTAINMENT, NOT OVERLAP. A construction whose capture
    type is a union overlaps a narrower arm and would route a ValueRef
    capture into a RawInt lane; the value's construction shape must be
    CONTAINED in the arm's shape (closure-literal subtyping). Element =
    a CallableShapes container mirroring TupleShapes, not a FiniteSet.
 3. AxisPrecision for callables = PerPosition recursing into captures;
    the covering seat then reorders a_mixed wide-first (sound; x23 dead
    -- fz-kdt.168).
 4. (A)'s cost is 55 canon movers / 11 fixtures gain executables / 0
    behaviour movers over 466 (fz-kdt.169), not R3's 3 splits.
 5. Interp boxes 32 direct-layout callables with a bare function id
    (fz-kdt.166); ClosureCapture carries wrapper identity_fns, not a
    CallableId (layering).
Staged as fz-kdt.127.1 (stage B) -> fz-kdt.127.2 (stage A); red-first
fixtures same_lambda_two_capture_types{,_dynamic}.fz; fz-kdt.167 owns the
union-capture containment fixture.

DESIGN, two populations, in the order the review proved:
 (B) DYNAMIC -- the WORD, first. For values no key can pin (a closure
     chosen by a runtime branch; a mailbox closure) the callable axis
     names the construction: CallableShapes over (target, captures:
     [RuntimeTypePredicate]) (fz-kdt.119's TupleShapes pattern,
     PerPosition); projection keeps lit.captures; each wrapper carries
     its projected shape; native ORs the wrappers whose construction is
     contained in the arm shape, interp compares shapes; ClosureCapture
     keyed by the minting wrappers. Deletions ride: the captures
     erasure, callable_boundaries_for_target + doc, NativeCallable
     Boundary.target, dead capture_key, the per-FnId agreement rule,
     the interp :2784 exemption, the "captures leave no trace" doctrine
     (dispatch-matrix.md:65-85 + precision row :270, types/mod.rs:1596,
     pipeline.md:29, fz-kdt.125's "one-boundary-per-FnId").
 (A) STATIC -- the KEY, second. The forwarder erasure erases the BRAND
     and keeps capture TYPES recursively. run gets one body per capture
     type, one twice target each, grounded direct, no dispatch node,
     zero runtime work. Needs a brand-less closure type form (~9 sites);
     the anonymous literal projects to CallableShapes::any() -- the one
     guard that makes A and B compose.
NOT the cure: consumer collapse (fz-6gb's "stop specializing"); a
capture-read runtime axis (rebuilds the word); generalization at minting
(refuted by prototype in 125); diagnostic backstop (refuses 5 fixtures).

POPULATIONS (census, 466 canon dumps at HEAD): 23 callables minted at
>1 capture layout across 12 fixtures. Same-layout/different-identity
captures (probeB1 4/9, probeB2 6/-6, 00281, the six residue groups) are
CORRECT today because those lambda bodies call the captured fn through
ITS word (target=-) and are byte-duplicates -- fz-kdt.163. The
type-differing population (sl3; 00411 without a forwarder) is the wrong
answer.

RELATIONS: fz-kdt.125 (the axis (B) refines; its "one boundary per
FnId" is false), fz-kdt.123 (closes when no-question groups are 0),
fz-kdt.157 (refusal witness becomes writable), fz-kdt.137 (depth-1
tuple hop; re-test after), fz-6gb (erasure narrowed by (A)), fz-kdt.152
(layout rule unchanged), fz-kdt.162/163/164/165 (bycatch).

ACCEPTANCE: (A) sl3 prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT, AOT, both orders,
red-first with an Elixir oracle, and run's callsite has NO dispatch node
(one target per run body); fz-6gb sharing census: 8 slots unchanged, the
3 splits classified; probeB1/B2/00411/pin6gb unchanged. (B) a red-first
dynamic witness (closure chosen by a runtime branch) correct on all
doors with a shape question; callsite_dispatch a_nested_callables_
captures_are_not_a_question FLIPS; residue gate 6 -> 0 or each survivor
named; 157's red witness; corpus canon movement classified; 3-door
behaviour sweep 0 movers except the new fixtures; docs rewritten.

## CHILDREN

- [ ] fz-kdt.127.1 P1 fz-kdt.127 stage B: the callable axis names the construction (CallableShapes, containment admission, PerPosition), construction-keyed capture unpack, on all three doors [blocks: fz-kdt.127.2, fz-kdt.166, fz-kdt.167, fz-kdt.168]
- [ ] fz-kdt.127.2 P1 fz-kdt.127 stage A: the forwarder erasure erases the brand and keeps capture types -- samelambda3 with zero dispatch nodes [blocks: fz-kdt.169] [blocked by: fz-kdt.127.1]

comments.text:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e). Two premises in
this ticket's body and in fz-kdt.125's spec item 6 are REFUTED:

(1) "13/13 in-corpus groups are identity-separable" is an artifact of the
census helper. Its separability test regexes EVERY closure/fnref name out of a
key, including the ones sitting in CAPTURES -- and a capture is not identity.
Re-measured against the landed axis: the no-question population falls 13 -> 6,
not 13 -> 0. The 6 survivors are THIS ticket's shape exactly, same fn id and
different captures:

  00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce      1  closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](fnref[add_a/2])
                                           vs (fnref[add_b/2])
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture              2  same lambda over two different inner closures
  00281_opaque_reducer_closure          1  as 00231
  behavior/opaque_fn_value_join         1  as 00231
  behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2  1  as 00277

(2) "Corpus fallout of the backstop measured ZERO" therefore does not hold. An
unrepresentable-plan DIAGNOSTIC on inseparable groups would refuse to compile
five corpus fixtures. The fz-kdt.125 build did NOT land it for that reason --
the routing half of this ticket is still open and still unbuilt, and it needs
either capture discrimination or a corpus that stops relying on the shape.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is this ticket's ABI half: `Prim::ClosureCapture` reads a
capture back out of a closure through the boundary that WROTE it, and refuses
at compile time when one callable was minted at several capture layouts that
disagree about a slot -- which is samelambda3's shape. That turns "native
executable lowering failed for index 11" into a named invariant failure. The
compile failure itself (interp: "omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is untouched and still this ticket's.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER, measured: 00281 with its twin function changed from
`acc + x` to `acc - x` answers -6 on interp and JIT at head. The six groups'
arm-0-takes-all is order-decided but the members are interchangeable on the
probes tried; that is luck, not a proof.

fz-kdt.119 review sequencing (2026-09-01): 119(3)'s recursive identity-preserving erasure ENLARGES this ticket's population ({:tag,#66(int)} vs {:tag,#66(float)} collapse to one question at depth -- same-fn-id/different-capture, one tuple deep). Also this ticket's compile-failure half now has a depth-1 instance with its own ticket (fz-kdt.137) which blocks 119's REFNEST-style acceptance. The backstop-policy decision this ticket owns grows correspondingly.
